In a recent development, while Cardinale did not confirm the imminent arrival of Markus Krösche – though he did admit to being in talks with him – his clear intention is to build a top-tier organisation. Cardinale’s goal is to lead Milan to a trophy – ideally the Scudetto – as early as this season.

Industry observers note that to do this, he knows strengthening the squad in January is a necessity. One name stands out in his notebook: Endrick, the forward at the moment with Real Madrid whom Mourinho – for the time being – is unwilling to let go of.

Regarding a potential move for the 20-year-old, Cardinale confirmed that the club like him: “Endrick’s name keeps coming up in the market. Our project goes beyond any single player, but Endrick is one of the best in the world – if not the best – considering his age and position. I have enormous respect for him, and we’ll see what might be possible.”.

In other words, the green light would need to be secured from Mourinho regarding his departure from Madrid. Milan know they can leverage the strong relationship between its owner and Roc Nation, the agency representing the Brazilian.

Industry observers note that given the business already conducted between RedBird and Roc Nation, it is likely that the player would favour Milan over other potential destinations. Meanwhile, Tresoldi has also piqued Cardinale’s interest, though he offers a different profile than Endrick.

Industry observers note that nicolo Tresoldi is also an option for the attack, but more significant progress has been made regarding the Brazilian. Bayern Munich are also watching the Club Brugge striker, with Harry Kane having undergone ankle surgery.

Industry observers note that in any case, Milan’s transfer activity will not be limited to a striker. Further arrivals will depend on the opportunities that arise during the winter window, with agents and intermediaries continually ringing the phone lines at Casa Milan.

There is a desire to bolster the defence, potentially with a central defender (possibly through the early return of Zachary Athekame, presently on loan at Lyon) and a left-sided player, should Pervis Estupiñán be sold.

Industry observers note that all of this is in addition to the contract renewal for Rabiot, the next player set to be secured following the agreements reached with Strahinja Pavlović and Christian Pulišić. In short, there is a lot in the works.

#95517. Tech Report: Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (901 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (901 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.
  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

According to recent reports, none of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

It has been revealed that with Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

Their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how swiftly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

True, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Recent findings suggest that still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of fresh players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

It has been revealed that ‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely crucial but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

It has been revealed that A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

Industry observers note that on this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

#95515. Breaking: Kroupi’s preferred destination ‘revealed’ as Bournemouth rule out January sale

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Kroupi’s preferred destination ‘revealed’ as Bournemouth rule out January sale

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (599 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 21:24.
  • In a recent development, barcelona may be ahead in the race for Eli Junior Kroupi, according to French outlet Foot Sur7, which reports that the 20-year-old Bournemouth forward would favour the Catalan club if he decides to leave the Premier League.
  • According to Foot Sur7, Kroupi has a special interest in playing for Barcelona, a possibility that had already been considered behind the scenes at the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 21:24.

In a recent development, barcelona may be ahead in the race for Eli Junior Kroupi, according to French outlet Foot Sur7, which reports that the 20-year-old Bournemouth forward would favour the Catalan club if he decides to leave the Premier League. Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal are also following the striker’s situation, but for now they are said to be behind Barcelona in the player’s preference.

According to Foot Sur7, Kroupi has a special interest in playing for Barcelona, a possibility that had already been considered behind the scenes at the club. Barcelona’s football department has followed the striker’s development since the last summer transfer window, and his name remains on sporting director Deco’s radar as an option to strengthen the attack in the coming years.

The Catalan interest also gains strength from information given by David Ornstein this week. Speaking on The Athletic FC podcast, the British journalist noted the Frenchman is weighing up leaving English football when he feels the time has come for a latest step in his career. A departure from the Premier League would put Barcelona and PSG in a favourable position, particularly if English rivals lose ground in the race.

Recent findings suggest that there is still no decision on the striker’s future, however. The preference for Barcelona reported by the French press does not mean a transfer is under way or that the player has made a final choice.

While Barcelona appear an attractive destination, Bournemouth are set to make any short-term move difficult. The English club are not planning to lose one of their main players in the January window and consider his presence important for their sporting goals.

It has been revealed that the position was reinforced by boss Marco Rose, who ruled out selling the forward in January. ‘For us, it is not a initiative to sell someone in January,’ Rose said. ‘It is not our plan and so far there are just rumours and noises.’.

Kroupi’s contract with Bournemouth also stands in the way of suitors. The striker is under contract until June 2030, which puts the Cherries in a comfortable position. With no need to release him immediately, they can set high conditions before opening talks. According to estimates in the British press, Bournemouth could ask for close to £100m to accept a transfer. That figure is a considerable barrier, particularly for Barcelona, who would need to weigh up the financial impact of an operation of this size.

Industry observers note that the interest is not explained solely by competition among European giants. At 20, Kroupi is already one of the most talked-about young names on the market, driven by his goalscoring ability, his versatility in attack and the room for improvement he still has. Those characteristics help explain why the Frenchman fits the profile Barcelona are seeking. The Catalan hierarchy are looking for alternatives who can add quality to the attack in the medium term, and the Bournemouth player has attributes that attract Deco and other members of the football department.

Industry observers note that PSG are also seen as a possible heavyweight rival, especially if the striker leaves English football. Arsenal are monitoring the situation, although according to Foot Sur7 they are behind Barcelona in Kroupi’s preference.

It has been revealed that A decision is not expected immediately. The striker intends to focus on recovering his best form this season before making any decision about a change of club, so next summer is the most likely time for a concrete assessment of his future.

Player to Watch: Pemi Aderoju (Crawley Town).

We controlled the first half and got off to a flyer, when Kai Jennings scored early after Fleetwood failed to deal with Kellan Gordon’s cross. We looked dangerous on the break all afternoon, with Dylan Morgan hitting the post before half-time, while Fleetwood barely created anything.

Right at the start of the second half, Morgan revealed brilliant vision to thread a lovely pass through the middle to find Pemi Aderoju, who smashed it home to make it 2-0, with Aderoju looking lively and causing all sorts of problems all game, and in my opinion, it was his best performance I’ve seen from him in a Crawley Town shirt.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Overall, this was a great all round performance, and even under pressure when Fleetwood got a goal back, we looked organised, confident, and quick on the break,  with the experience of players like Ben Heneghan really showing in this match, with him putting in some crucial blocks, and if he stays fit, he will really add to our defence.

This wraps up a pretty positive week for the Red Devils, and this win puts us back within touching distance of 22nd-placed Rochdale, with us being just three points off, and with high-flying Barnet visiting the Broadfield on Tuesday night, there is still a lot of work to do, but Kevin Blackwell remains unbeaten in the league, and hopefully this is the start of a real revival, fingers crossed.

From FA Cup embarrassment to Fleetwood triumph – Crawley Town fans have reason to smile

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Before the game against Fleetwood, Kevin Blackwell was made “permanent” manager, at least until the end of the season, and the general feeling around Broadfield Stadium before the game was that it was the right thing to do in the position we find ourselves in at the moment.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“It’s a funny old game football”, as Greavesy would have mentioned back in the day, although I don’t think he meant comical, more like funny peculiar. Having been knocked out of the FA Cup by Wimborne, a team three divisions below League Two, although if you’re going to nit-pick, it’s actually, two divisions and a bit as it stands at the moment between us and them, we have now beaten the team that dumped the current Premier League Champions out of the Carabao Cup.

Before the game against Fleetwood, Kevin Blackwell was made “permanent” manager, at least until the end of the season, and the general feeling around Broadfield Stadium before the game was that it was the right thing to do in the position we find ourselves in at the moment.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The atmosphere in the stadium, right from the kick off, was excellent and it was made even better when Kai Jennings scored after just five minutes in front of a segregated North stand with half of it being given over to home supporters.

As expected, Fleetwood began to get into the game, but the presence of Josh Flint and Ben Heneghan as central defenders and playing Danilo Orsi AND Pemi Aderoju up front together gave Crawley a totally different more attacking outlook.

In a recent development, scoring early after the half time break certainly helps, and if we had scored a third, no one could have noted it wouldn’t have been deserved. Two nil leads carry with them a certain tension and when the Cod Army pulled a goal back with eleven minutes to go it almost seemed inevitable that fate would deliver us yet another cruel blow. This time however, the boys in Red saw it through to the very end and thoroughly deserved the heart felt appreciation given to them by the home support.

There were only two League Two games scheduled for last night (if  you’re reading this on Wednesday morning.) Our home game against second in the division, Barnet , but the other game being played will also affect us, as it is between Port Vale and Northampton, who have six more points than Crawley, but have played one and two games more than us respectively. The best outcome for me would be for us to beat Barnet and for the other game to be a draw. I’ll leave you to do the Maths.

On the Red Devils’ Diary front things are going well and we have no intends to increase the cost from £2, or rather we didn’t have, but in conjunction with the club’s announcement of their 130th anniversary week events beginning on Monday 7th December and culminating with our current players playing against Newport County on Saturday the 12th in a special one-off kit reminiscent of the 1896 one worn by our founders, we will be producing a souvenir edition for the Newport game which will feature messages from and pen pics of ex-players and will also feature so much more inside for a  once only cost of just £3,  If you haven’t bought a ricket for the Wednesday night event yet, when ex-players will be present to take your questions and you will get a chance to have a glimpse at the first CTFC MUSEUM exhibition, then why not?

Onwards and upwards. Red4ever, that’s  me!
